record.paper_title: Open Questions in Massive Star Research across Cosmic Scales
record.original_question: How can high-redshift massive-star observations, which are limited in spatial resolution and wavelength coverage, be robustly connected to the underlying physical processes using a ladder of local analogs and testbed environments? The needed program must link nearby low-metallicity dwarf galaxies, unresolved and resolved clusters, and individual stellar systems, so that detailed stellar physics and population-synthesis constraints can be tied back to integrated high-redshift observations.

evidence.quote: While yielding fascinating new discoveries, high-redshift observations alone will be insufficient to answer any of these questions robustly as the resolution and wavelength regimes are quite limited. A whole ladder of local analogs and testbed environments is required to study and connect the involved physical processes, ranging from nearby (dwarf) galaxies with lower Z over unresolved and resolved clusters to individual stellar systems such as the iron-poor O stars in the Magellanic Bridge (Schösser et al. 2025).

Resolved clusters are a particular important step as individual stars can be studied in detail while the cluster environment yields additional constraints and provides a testbed for population synthesis.

artifact.status_search_result: This is a broad open research-program question in massive-star astrophysics rather than a closed mathematical problem. Current literature on low-metallicity massive stars, resolved-cluster spectroscopy, and population-synthesis calibration (e.g. ULLYSES/XShootU surveys, Magellanic Bridge O-star studies) treats the construction of such a local-to-high-z ladder as an active, ongoing program with no agreed-upon complete solution.

status_evidence.title: ULLYSES: A Hubble Space Telescope UV Legacy Library of Young Stars
status_evidence.snippet: ULLYSES provides UV spectra of low-metallicity massive stars in the Magellanic Clouds as local analogs for high-redshift stellar populations.
status_evidence.claim: The construction of a local low-Z analog library for high-z massive-star populations is presented as ongoing community effort.

status_evidence.title: XShootU: A ULLYSES complementary survey
status_evidence.snippet: XShootU provides optical spectroscopy complementing ULLYSES to calibrate stellar atmosphere and population-synthesis models at low metallicity.
status_evidence.claim: Cross-calibration of stellar physics and population synthesis using local low-Z testbeds remains an active, unfinished program.
